key_insight: TCMClinicalReason-Bench shows that LLMs can produce complete-looking TCM case responses while still lacking patient-grounded reasoning from pathogenesis to prescription.
clinical_relevance: For TCM clinical decision support, this benchmark highlights where models may need human oversight most: prescription generation, prescription analysis, and symptom-guided modification.
method: Built a 2,000-case multicenter benchmark from real electronic health records.
Evaluated five general-purpose and two TCM-specific LLMs in zero-shot settings.
Used an evidence-constrained rubric covering seven components and three cross-block relations, with automated judging and blinded clinician review.
evidence_signal: Across models, structural completeness was near ceiling (99.3%-100.0%), but normalized content scores were much lower (40.7%-54.1%) and cross-block consistency was only moderate (60.8%-66.8%).
watch_item: High completeness can mask unsupported reasoning, so deployment should pair model outputs with clinician review rather than rely on endpoint scores alone.
paper_title: TCMClinicalReason-Bench: Can Language Models Reason from Pathogenesis to Prescription over Real-World Clinical Cases?
